REFERRED TO NEW YORK CITY EDUCATION
AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO NEW YORK CITY EDUCATION

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to requiring class size
reduction plans in city school districts in cities having a population of one
million or more
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6296

SPONSOR: JACKSON
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the education law, in relation to requiring class size
reduction plans in city school districts in cities having a population
of one million or more

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this legislation is to implement a class size reduction
plan in the New York City school district.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends subparagraphs (ii) and (iii) of paragraph b of subdivi-
sion 2 of Section 211-D of the Education Law. This will require the
school district in a city with a population of one million or more to
have a plan to reduce citywide average class sizes by district and
school beginning in September 2021 and to be achieved by September 2026
for grade ranges pre-kindergarten through 3rd grade, 4th grade through
8th grade, and high school; and thereafter maintain average class sizes
achieved by September 2026.

The city school district shall prepare annual reports on the plan to
reduce average class sizes and the report shall be made readily avail-
able to the public through the city school district's website.  The
report must also identify all schools that received funds targeted at
class size reduction efforts. The report needs to detail the actual
student enrollment for school years 2020-2021, 2021-2022, 2022-2023,
2023-2024, and 2024-2025, and the projected student enrollment for
2025-2026; the average class size for 2020-2021, 2021-2022, 2022-2023,
and the projected class sizes for 2023-2023, and thereafter until the
class size goals are achieved. The report also needs to include the
annual capital plan for school construction and leasing to show how many
classrooms will be added in each year and in which schools and subdis-
tricts to achieve the class size reduction goals. Further, the report
also needs to include the school capacity and utilization formula is
aligned to the class size goals.

The first report needs to be submitted to the commissioner of education
on or before November 15 of each year. If the department determines that
the report does show sufficient decreases in class size, the city school
district shall submit a plan for corrective action.

Section 2 is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The children of New York City have waited far too long to receive educa-
tional justice. For decades overcrowded classrooms have impaired
students' ability to learn, build relationships with their teachers and
other staff. This bill will update Contracts for Excellence in New York
City to help change that situation for the more than one million chil-
dren in the care of Department of education schools.  Class size direct-
ly impacts student success and as schools reopen from COVID-19 closures,
campuses will increase capacity while navigating health and safety

protocols. This bill will help alleviate historically damaging condi-
tions to better serve students.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
STATE AND LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately; provided, however that the
amendments to section 211-d of the education law made by section one of
this act shall first apply to contracts for excellence for the 2021-2022
school year.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6296A

SPONSOR: JACKSON
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the education law, in relation to requiring class size
reduction plans in city school districts in cities having a population
of one million or more

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this legislation is to implement a class size reduction
plan in the New York City school district.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends paragraph e of subdivision 1 of Section 211-D of the
Education Law to require that a school district that submitted a
contract for excellence in academic year 2021-2022 must submit a
contract for excellence for academic year 2022-2023 unless all schools
in the district are in good standing.

Section 2 amends subparagraphs (ii) and (iii) of paragraph b of subdivi-
sion 2 of Section 211-D of the Education Law. This will require the
school district in a city with a population of one million or more to
have a plan to reduce citywide average class sizes by district and
school beginning in September 2022 and to be achieved by September 2027
for grade ranges pre-kindergarten through 3rd grade, 4th grade through
8th grade, and high school; and thereafter maintain average class sizes
achieved by September 2026.

The city school district shall prepare annual reports on the plan to
reduce average class sizes and the report shall be made readily avail-
able to the public through the city school district's website.  The
report must also identify all schools that received funds targeted at
class size reduction efforts. The report needs to detail the actual
student enrollment for school years 2022-2023, 2023-2024, 2024-2025,
2025-2026, and 2026-2027, and the projected student enrollment for
2026-2027; the average class size for 2023-2024, 2024-2025, 2025-2026,
and the projected class sizes for 2026-2027, and thereafter until the
class size goals are achieved. The report also needs to include the
annual capital plan for school construction and leasing to show how many
classrooms will be added in each year and in which schools and subdis-
tricts to achieve the class size reduction goals.  Further, the report
also needs to include the school capacity and utilization formula is
aligned to the class size goals.

The first report needs to be submitted to the commissioner of education
on or before November 15 of each year. If the department determines that
the report does show sufficient decreases in class size, the city school
district shall submit a plan for corrective action.

Section 3 amends paragraph d of subdivision 4 and subdivision 5 of
Section 211-D of the Education Law. This requires the public process for
commenting on the proposed plan shall commence no later than 30 days
after the state budget is enacted and must be completed 30 days after
the public process begins. Notice of the public comment process to be
given 15 days prior to the commencement of the public process.  This
notice must be posted on the school district's website as well as be
transmitted via email to school administrators, parent and teacher
organizations, and elected officials. Additionally, the proposed plan
shall be submitted for state approval within two weeks following the
completion of the public process. The proposed plan must be posted on
the school district's website within 24 hours of submission along with a
summary of the public comments and the school district's explanation and
reasons for which public comments were incorporated into the proposed
plan and which public comments were not incorporated into the proposed
plan.

Contract for excellence shall be approved and the corresponding funds
released once the public process has been completed. The approved plan
shall be posted on the department's website within 48 hours after its
approval along with any revisions to such plan or corrective action
required by the state. Contract for excellence funds shall be released
to the school district when the contract is approved by the commission-
er. Upon approval of the contract for excellence, one-third of the funds
shall be released to the school district. The remaining funds shall be
released to the school district upon submission of the commissioner's
report by November 15, only if the report demonstrates sufficient
reduction in class sizes.  If the report does not reflect sufficient
class size reduction, the remaining funds shall be released upon
submission of a corrective action plan.

Section 4 is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The children of New York City have waited far too long to receive educa-
tional justice. For decades overcrowded classrooms have impaired
students' ability to learn, build relationships with their teachers and
other staff. This bill will update Contracts for Excellence in New York
City to help change that situation for the more than one million chil-
dren in the care of Department of education schools.  Class size direct-
ly impacts student success and as schools reopen from COVID-19 closures,
campuses will increase capacity while navigating health and safety
protocols. This bill will help alleviate historically damaging condi-
tions to better serve students.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
STATE AND LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately and shall first apply to
contracts for excellence for the 2022-2023 school year.

summary: Requires city school districts in cities having a population of one million or more to develop class size reduction plans beginning in September 2022 to reduce the average classroom size citywide, by district, and by school in such districts by the 2027-2028 school year.
